newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance delays filing report.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance delays filing report.

text.p: Mercury Finance Co, the beleaguered consumer finance company, said it will not file its 1996 form 10-K annual report with the Securities and Exchange Commission on time and does not know when it will be filed.
In a filing with the SEC late Tuesday, Mercury said it was unable to determine the required information due to accounting irregularities and related matters.
The company said in January it would have to lower its reported earnings over the last four years by about $90 million, due to accounting irregularities.

Since then, Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt, been served with a search warrant by FBI agents seeking financial records and has been named a defendant in more than half a dozen lawsuits surrounding the misstated earnings. The company also lost more than $2 billion in market capitalization when the stock plunged following its report that it would slash its reported earnings.
Mercury hired Arthur Anderson LLP as its new auditor and a company spokesman said last month the audit of its 1996 financial results was not likely to be completed until May.
Mercury shares were unchanged at 2-1/2 Wednesday.
